important.name: working SKILL.md routes the `--` tail into the refs, against the guidance-tail rule it cites
important.summary:
The skill's argument-hint `-- <todo-id|#issue>... | --clear | --list` (line 4) and its table row `-- <todo-id|#issue>...` stores the refs (line 17) treat text after a standalone `--` as refs. Lines 22-24 then say the split follows `reference/skill_arguments.md` and that guidance never reaches the command line. That reference (lines 14-20) makes the tail after `--` guidance for every skill whose own arguments are not free text, and the root README (line 211) lists only `c-msg`, `check-runlogs` and `add-bookmark` as skills where a leading `--` is optional. Refs are ids, not free text. So `/harness:working -- todo-k69m`, the shape the hint advertises, reads as no own arguments (the usage line) under the cited rule but as a set under the skill's table. `/harness:working todo-k69m -- only the banner` gives no rule for the tail: the first-word table (lines 38-43) maps it to `WORKING set` with every token, and `parse_refs` then refuses `only` with exit 1. The add-bookmark shape the plan copied works only because add-bookmark states its free-text exemption (its lines 22-24) and has a leading-`--` row in its first-word table; working has neither.

Also (docs): The description (line 3, "overriding what the branch name and its plan say") and the body (lines 9-10, "By default they come from the branch name and its plan") name the branch name as a source of refs. The mod builds the refs from the union of the qualifying plans' `refs` only (`plugins/working-refs/hooks/line.ts:41-44`), and a plan qualifies by its `branch` field or by its `base_commit` matching the merge base (`plans.ts:103-110`). The branch name contributes no ref. Line 10-11 also calls the file "per project", but `working.py:33` stores it under the checkout's `state_dir`, and the mod README (line 71) says each worktree has its own.

Also (skill_package): The arguments table (working/SKILL.md:17) and argument-hint (line 4) say `-- <todo-id|#issue>...` stores the refs, while lines 21-24 cite skill_arguments.md, under which everything after a standalone `--` is guidance that never reaches the command line. That reference only makes a leading `--` optional for skills whose own arguments are free text; refs are not free text, and this body never claims the exception (add-bookmark states it outright at its SKILL.md:23). The hint also passes test_hint_advertises_the_guidance_tail only because it contains `-- <`, not because the skill has a guidance tail, so `/harness:working todo-k69m -- <guidance>` has no stated meaning.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:4 advertises `-- <todo-id|#issue>... | --clear | --list` and the table at SKILL.md:17 treats `-- <todo-id|#issue>...` as a set, while SKILL.md:22-24 (and reference/skill_arguments.md:14-16,33-35) say everything after the first standalone `--` is guidance that 'never reaches the command line'. The free-text exception (skill_arguments.md:19-20) that lets add-bookmark use `-- <note text>` covers free text, not ids. `/harness:working todo-k69m -- focus on X` has no defined parse: the table's 'anything else' row would pass every word. The hint shape was chosen in TASK-3 to satisfy the `-- <` check of test_skill_guidance_tail_contract.py:56-58, so the skill now advertises a guidance tail it never applies.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:3 ('overriding what the branch name and its plan say') and SKILL.md:9-10 ('By default they come from the branch name and its plan') claim that refs are derived from the branch name. The mod's buildLine (plugins/working-refs/hooks/line.ts:37-47) takes refs only from the override or the union of the qualifying plans' `refs`; the branch name only selects the override and rule 1 of qualifies (plans.ts:103-110). The working-refs README (README.md:12-13) states it correctly.

Also (roast): The argument-hint and the Arguments table say `-- <todo-id|#issue>...` stores the refs. The next paragraph says the guidance split follows skill_arguments.md and that 'the guidance never reaches the command line', and under that rule text after `--` is guidance. The routing table has no row for a leading `--` or for `--` alone. add-bookmark, whose shape this skill copies, says outright that a leading `--` is dropped and that the rest is always the payload. This skill leaves the agent to guess.

Also (roast): The working SKILL.md says that by default the refs 'come from the branch name and its plan', and its description says the override is 'overriding what the branch name and its plan say'. The mod never reads refs from the branch name. buildLine takes the union of the qualifying plans' `refs`, and the branch only decides which plans qualify (rule 1, or rule 2 by merge base). A reader will look for a branch-name parser that doesn't exist.
fix: Treat the `--` tail as guidance: set the hint to `"<todo-id|#issue>... | --clear | --list [-- <guidance>]"` (it still holds `-- <`, which the guidance-tail test checks), drop the `-- <todo-id|#issue>...` form from the line 17 row, and state that only the arguments before a standalone `--` become `WORKING set` tokens; add a first-word row where `--` alone or first prints the usage line.

Or keep the hint and declare the add-bookmark exemption: say that a leading `--` is dropped and the rest are tokens, that a later `--` starts guidance which never reaches `set`, add the leading-`--` row to the first-word table, and add `working` to the free-text list in README.md line 211.

Line 3: "overriding the refs of the plans that qualify for the branch". Lines 9-11: "By default they are the union of the `refs` of the plans that qualify for the branch (its own plan, or a plan whose base commit is the branch's merge base); an override set here replaces them for that branch only. The file is per checkout (`<state_dir>/working-refs/overrides.json`)..."

In working/SKILL.md after line 24, state the rule explicitly as add-bookmark does: a leading `--` is optional and everything after it is refs; a later standalone `--` starts guidance, and only the tokens before it reach `WORKING set`.

Set the hint to `<todo-id|#issue>... | --clear | --list [-- <guidance>]`, drop the `or -- <todo-id|#issue>...` alternative from SKILL.md:17, and state that only the words before a standalone `--` become tokens.
Reword SKILL.md:3 and 9-10 to say the refs default to the union of the `refs` of the plans that qualify for the branch (its own plan, or one written against its merge base).

Copy add-bookmark's wording: 'the tokens are the whole value, so a leading `--` is dropped', add the rows 'a leading `--` -> WORKING set <rest>' and 'nothing (or `--` alone) -> usage line', and drop the sentence saying guidance never reaches the command line, or reword it to match.

Reword both places: 'By default they are the union of the `refs` of the plans that qualify for the branch (its own plan, or a plan written at its merge base); an override set here replaces them for that branch only.'

important.name: Unquoted #N tokens become shell comments in the working and write-plan commands
important.summary:
working/SKILL.md:42 maps the arguments to `WORKING set <token>...`, each token as a separate argument, with no quoting rule, and line 21 names `#301` as a valid token. In the Bash tool an unquoted word starting with `#` begins a comment, so `/harness:working todo-k69m #301` (the README.md:182 example) runs `set todo-k69m`: #301 is silently dropped and fill_issues replaces it with the catalog's gh_issues. `/harness:working #301` runs `set` with no tokens, an argparse usage error (exit 2), not the documented `working:` line. write-plan/SKILL.md:36-38 has the same hole: `--refs` takes comma- or space-separated tokens (plan.py nargs='+'), so `--refs todo-k69m #301` loses the issue and `--refs #301` fails in argparse. The add-bookmark skill this one copies quotes its argument in single quotes (add-bookmark/SKILL.md:61).

Also (overall): SKILL.md routes every other first word to `WORKING set <token>...`, each token as a separate argument, and the skill's own examples use `#301`. The Bash tool runs Git Bash, where a word that starts with `#` opens a comment: `... working.py set todo-k69m #301` drops `#301` without a message. fill_issues then sees no issue and fills the issues from the catalog, so the stored override differs from what the developer typed. `... working.py set #301` gets no tokens at all, and argparse exits 2 with a usage error instead of the documented `working:` line. tests/skills/test_working_script.py calls main() with a list, so no shell is involved and the tests cannot catch this. The same trap applies to `plan.py new --refs`, whose docstring and the write-plan step advertise space-separated tokens (`--refs todo-k69m #301` loses the issue).

Also (system_shape): plugins/harness/skills/working/SKILL.md:42 tells the agent to run `WORKING set <token>...`, 'each token as a separate argument', and the README (README.md:182, 189) and the skill (SKILL.md:21) advertise `#301` as the issue form. Through the Bash tool, a word that starts with `#` after whitespace begins a comment: `sh .../hpy .../working.py set todo-k69m #301` runs `set todo-k69m` only. working.py then sees no issue, fill_issues (working_refs.py:78-87) fills the issues from the catalog instead, and the script prints success, so the developer's explicit issue is silently replaced or lost. The same applies to `plan.py new --refs todo-k69m #301` in the space-separated form the docstring allows (plan.py:248-251, write-plan SKILL.md step 1 says 'comma- or space-separated'). The tests call main() with a Python list (tests/skills/test_working_script.py:44,53) and so cannot see it.

Also (roast): The working skill routes everything else to `WORKING set <token>...`, each token as a separate argument, through the Bash tool, and gives `#301` as the issue form. In bash a word that starts with `#` begins a comment, so `... working.py set todo-k69m #301` runs as `set todo-k69m`. The issue is dropped with no error. Then `fill_issues` sees no issue and fills in the catalog's `gh_issues`, so the stored override quietly differs from what the developer typed. The write-plan step 1 hint `--refs <todo ids and issues>`, with `plan.py --refs` documented as space-separated, has the same trap for a space-separated `#N`. Most banners don't silently rewrite their input; this one does.

Also (overall): The argument-hint and the arguments table accept `-- <todo-id|#issue>...`, but the 'First word' routing table has no row for a leading `--`, for `--` alone, or for a `-- guidance` tail after the tokens. The add-bookmark table this skill copies covers all three. skill_arguments.md treats a leading `--` as optional only for skills whose arguments are free text, and these arguments are ids, so whether the text after `--` is refs or guidance is left to the session. Passing `--` or the guidance words into `set` makes parse_refs refuse them.
fix: In working/SKILL.md line 42, say each token goes on the command line in single quotes (`WORKING set 'todo-k69m' '#301'`), and add a one-line example; in write-plan/SKILL.md step 1, write the flag as `--refs '<todo ids and issues>'` with the example `--refs 'todo-k69m,#301'`.

In working/SKILL.md, require each token to be single-quoted on the command line (`WORKING set 'todo-k69m' '#301'`) and say why; in write-plan/SKILL.md step 1, quote the `--refs` value or keep the comma form only.
Or tell the session to pass issues as bare numbers (drop the leading `#`; parse_refs already accepts `301`), and note it in both SKILL.md files.

SKILL.md:42: change the row to `WORKING set <token>...`, each token as a separate single-quoted argument (`'#301'`): an unquoted word starting with `#` is a shell comment. Add the same note to the write-plan SKILL.md step 1 `--refs` sentence and to plan.py's `new` docstring (or show only the comma form `todo-k69m,#301`, where `#` is mid-word).
Have the skill strip a leading `#` from issue tokens before building the command (the parser already accepts `301`), and say so in SKILL.md.
In working SKILL.md, require each token to be single-quoted on the command line (`WORKING set 'todo-k69m' '#301'`), and say why: bash reads a leading `#` as a comment.

Alternatively, have the skill join the tokens with commas into one single-quoted argument (`WORKING set 'todo-k69m,#301'`), which parse_refs already splits; do the same in write-plan step 1 (`--refs 'todo-k69m,#301'`).

Add routing rows: a leading `--` is dropped and the rest are tokens; `--` alone prints the usage line; for any other standalone `--`, only the words before it are tokens and the rest is guidance that never reaches the command.

important.name: The git-status snapshot trigger has no test; the test named for it exercises the prompt fallback
important.summary: Plan TASK-5 lists 'a branch change in git-status's snapshot' as a scan trigger. The code for it is the `state.set` hook on `{plugin: 'git-status', key: 'git'}` plus onSnapshot (watch.ts:359-363, 375-381). The test named 'a branch change in git-status's snapshot rescans' (watch.test.ts:357-367) changes `w.git` underneath and then submits a prompt. Its own comment says the engine refuses a test's `$.state.set`. So the rescan comes from onPrompt's branch comparison (watch.ts:348), and neither onSnapshot nor the state.set hook runs in any test. If either broke, for example a wrong key in the filter or a `branch === memo.branch` check that never matches, the suite would stay green. The banner would then refresh only at the next prompt.
fix: Export the snapshot decision as a pure function (e.g. `isSnapshotMove(memo, branch)` or a `branchOfSnapshot(value)` plus the comparison), unit-test it for a same branch, another branch, a null snapshot and an unscanned memo, and rename watch.test.ts:357 to 'a branch change seen at the next prompt rescans'.
If the testing engine offers a route to dispatch a git-status-owned `state.set` (a hook registered as that plugin), drive onSnapshot through it and assert the line changes without a prompt.

important.name: The 'unchanged line is not written again' test never reaches a second write attempt
important.summary: The test at watch.test.ts:416-423 starts a scan, then sends a prompt and a Bash call and asserts one write. In this world neither probe starts a rescan: onPrompt (watch.ts:347-357) sees the same branch, HEAD, tags, plans signature and override mtime, and afterToolCall (watch.ts:336-340) sees no file move. writeLineFile (watch.ts:277-280) therefore runs once, and its compare-before-write check is never tested for a non-empty line. If that check were removed, the test would still pass. The empty-line case is covered elsewhere (watch.test.ts:295-302, 408-414). The test proves that probes skip needless rescans, which is not the behavior its name claims.
fix: Force a rescan that renders the same text before the assertion, e.g. rewrite the plan with identical content at a newer mtime (`w.setFile(<plan path>, planJson(), NOW - 1_000)`) or write an override for another branch, then call `bash($, w)` and assert `w.writes.length === 1` and `w.gits` grew (proving a scan ran).
Rename the test to what it checks now ('an unmoved world runs no rescan and no write') and add a separate test that forces the same-text rescan.

important.name: No test covers `working set` filling issues from the TODO catalog
important.summary: Plan TASK-3 says `set` fills issues from the TODO catalog the same way `plan.py new` does. working.py reads the catalog and calls fill_issues (working.py:31-32, 49-51). Every test in test_working_script.py uses a project with no `todo` config, so `catalog` is always `{}`. The `cfg.todo.catalog` / read_json branch never runs, and the wiring into fill_issues is never checked. `plan.py new` has the matching test (test_plan_new_refs.py:46-50). The working command, whose override replaces the plan refs in the banner, does not, so a regression that drops the filled issues would pass.
fix: Add `test_set_fills_issues_from_the_todo_catalog` to test_working_script.py: build the project with `{"todo": {"folder": "docs/TODO"}}`, write `docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json` mapping todo-k69m to [301] (as `_with_catalog` does in test_plan_new_refs.py:29-37), run `set todo-k69m`, and assert the stored issues are [301] and stdout holds 'todo-k69m (301)'.

minor.summary:
Step 4 (lines 58-65) tells the skill to replace the `.claude/state/harness` part of the widget's `commandPath` with `state_dir`. The command joins it with `require('path').join(r, ...)` (ccstatusline.defaults.json third line). `state_dir` may be absolute (the mod's `config.ts:52-57` keeps an absolute one, as `cfg.path()` does). `path.join` does not reset at an absolute segment, so `E:/proj` joined with `D:/state/working-refs/line.txt` names a path that does not exist, and the widget's `catch` prints nothing with no sign of the failure. A Windows `state_dir` written with backslashes would also land inside a single-quoted JS string inside a JSON string, where each backslash is an escape. The banner-status README bullet (lines 312-313) repeats the rule without the limit.

Also (roast): The mod writes line.txt under the first folder at or above the session cwd that holds `.claude/harness.json` (or under an absolute `state_dir` as given). The widget reads `path.join(workspace.project_dir || cwd, '<state_dir>/working-refs/line.txt')`. With an absolute `state_dir`, setup-statusline step 4 splices the absolute path into `path.join(r, ...)`, which gives `<project>\D:\state\...`, and the mod's file is also shared across worktrees, which contradicts the README's 'each worktree has its own line'. With a session launched in a subfolder of the project, project_dir is that subfolder while the mod writes at the project root. Either way the widget prints nothing.

Also (overall, system_shape): The widget command builds the file path as `require('path').join(r, '<state_dir>/working-refs/line.txt')`, and setup-statusline step 4 substitutes the configured `state_dir` into it. path.join concatenates, so an absolute `state_dir` (which harness `cfg.path()` and the mod's `under()` in hooks/config.ts both accept) becomes `<project>/D:/state/...`. A Windows `state_dir` written with backslashes also breaks once placed in a JS single-quoted string inside JSON (`\s` turns into `s`). In both cases the widget prints nothing while the mod writes the file elsewhere.

Also (system_shape): setup-statusline SKILL.md:58-62 and the banner-status README (README.md:38-39) say the skill substitutes the configured `state_dir` into the widget's commandPath. The command (ccstatusline.defaults.json:33) builds the path with `require('path').join(r, '<state_dir>/working-refs/line.txt')`. path.join concatenates an absolute second argument under `r` (`E:/proj/E:/state/...`), so with an absolute `state_dir` the widget reads a missing file and prints nothing. The harness (`cfg.path`) and the mod (config.ts:56-57 `under`, tested in overrides.test.ts:69-72) both accept an absolute `state_dir`.
fix: Use `require('path').resolve(r, '<state_dir>/working-refs/line.txt')` in the defaults' command (resolve keeps an absolute second argument), and have step 4 write `state_dir` with forward slashes; update the README bullet to match.
Or keep `join` and have step 4 refuse or warn on an absolute `state_dir`, writing a relative one with forward slashes only; say so in the README bullet.

In setup-statusline step 4, when `state_dir` is absolute, replace the whole `path.join(r,'...')` argument with the absolute file path. Note in the working-refs README Files section that an absolute state_dir is shared by every checkout.
Optionally, have the widget command walk up from project_dir to the first folder holding `.claude/harness.json`, the same root rule the mod uses.

Use `require('path').resolve(r, '...')` in the defaults' commandPath (the contract test's `f"{state_dir}/{LINE_REL}" in commandPath` assertion still holds), and have SKILL.md step 4 write `state_dir` with forward slashes.

In ccstatusline.defaults.json:33, use `require('path').resolve(r, '...')`: resolve keeps an absolute second argument and joins a relative one. No test changes needed, since test_setup_statusline_contract.py checks only the substring and project_dir.

minor.name: Issue numbers: plan refs and override refs follow different rules
minor.summary:
`PlanRefs.issues` is `List[StrictInt]` with no lower bound, so plan_api.write or a hand-edited override file can store 0, a negative number or a duplicate. The mod reads the two sources differently. plans.ts `uniqueIssues` keeps only positive integers and drops duplicates. overrides.ts `isWhole` (`Number.isInteger`) keeps 0, negatives and duplicates. The same `issues` list can therefore show one way when it comes from a plan and another way when it comes from an override, and Python's `format_refs` prints whatever the model accepted (`#0`, `#-5`). `parse_refs` only produces positive numbers, so this happens only for values written another way.

Also (overall): PlanRefs.issues is List[StrictInt], so a plan written through plan_api.write can carry `issues: [0, -3]`. parse_refs never produces those, and plans.ts uniqueIssues filters them out (n > 0), so a validated plan holds values the banner silently ignores.
fix: Bound the model: `issues: List[Annotated[StrictInt, Field(gt=0)]]` on PlanRefs, which read_overrides already skips on ValidationError, and in overrides.ts make `isWhole` require `n > 0`, matching plans.ts.
Or leave the model as it is and make overrides.ts filter and de-duplicate with the same rule as plans.ts `uniqueIssues`, so both sources render the same way.
Constrain the items to positive integers (`List[Annotated[StrictInt, Field(gt=0)]]`) and regenerate ActionPlan.schema.json with tools/gen_plan_schema.py.

minor.name: An empty ref set is stored as an override

The mod's buildLine treats that empty override as replacing the plans' refs, which silently blanks the refs part of the line for the branch.
fix: In parse_refs, raise WorkingRefsError('no TODO id or issue number given') when both lists end up empty; plan.py new and working.py already turn that into a refusal.

minor.name: plan.py reimplements the TODO catalog read that working.py takes from todo_sync
minor.summary:
D7 fills issues from the catalog in two places, and each reads the file its own way. `catalog_json()` in plan.py reads and parses the file by hand (json.loads, catching OSError and ValueError, then an isinstance(dict) check). working.py `context()` calls `harness_lib.todo_sync.sources.read_json`, which already returns the parsed object, or an error for an absent, unparseable or non-object file. The two readers do the same job, so a later change to how the catalog resolves or validates (an absolute catalog path, an encoding fallback, a schema check) has to be made in both or `plan.py new --refs` and `/harness:working set` drift apart.

Also (overall, system_shape): plan.py adds catalog_json(), its own json.loads of `active().path(todo.catalog)`. working.py context() reads the same file through todo_sync.sources.read_json. TASK-3 asks `set` to fill issues 'as plan.py new does', but the two paths can disagree on an unreadable or non-object catalog.

Also (system_shape): plan.py adds catalog_json() (plan.py:281-290: active().todo.catalog, active().path(), json.loads, dict check), while working.py's context() (working.py:23-33) reads the same file through todo_sync.sources.read_json. TASK-3 says `set` fills issues 'as plan.py new does'. Each new caller of fill_issues now has to pick one of two readers, and their edge cases can drift (an absolute catalog path, an unreadable file).
fix: Add one helper to harness_lib/working_refs.py, such as `catalog_of(cfg) -> Dict[str, Any]` built on `todo_sync.sources.read_json(cfg.project_root, cfg.todo.catalog)` that returns {} when the key is unset or the read fails. Call it from plan.py `new_refs` and from working.py `context`, and delete `catalog_json`.
Or have plan.py `catalog_json` call `read_json(active().project_root, catalog)` and return `found.data if found.ok else {}`, like working.py does.
Move one `catalog_data(cfg)` helper into harness_lib.working_refs, built on read_json, and call it from both plan.py new_refs and working.py context.
Add a `catalog_data(cfg) -> Dict[str, Any]` helper to harness_lib.working_refs (or reuse read_json there) and call it from both plan.py new_refs and working.py context; delete plan.py's catalog_json.

The plan.py docstring ('a TODO id given with no issue takes its gh_issues'), write-plan SKILL.md step 1 ('an id given with no issue takes its issue') and the v1.0.0 release line ('a TODO id named without an issue') read as a per-id rule. The harness README (README.md:191-192, 'When no token is an issue') and the working SKILL (SKILL.md:21-22) state the real rule.

The root README (lines 193-194) and the working SKILL.md (lines 21-22) state the rule correctly: "when no token names an issue". The plan.py docstring (lines 27-29, outside this bucket) repeats the per-id wording.
fix: Reword the three texts to 'when no token is an issue number, the issues come from the named ids' gh_issues in the TODO catalog'.
Reword the three texts to the README form: when no token is an issue number, the issues come from the named TODO ids' `gh_issues` in the catalog.

minor.name: Mod and widget pick the checkout by different rules (cwd first vs project_dir first)
minor.summary: watch.ts resolveWatch tries the session cwd and the folders above it first, then CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. The widget reads `workspace.project_dir` first, then `cwd`. In a session launched in the main checkout whose cwd moves into a linked worktree, the mod writes the worktree's line.txt, so band-line shows the worktree's line, while ccstatusline reads the main checkout's line.txt, which holds a stale line or none. banner-status README and SKILL.md step 4 promise that 'each worktree session prints its own checkout's line', and that holds only when the session was launched in that worktree.
fix: Make both sides use one rule: either the widget prefers `j.cwd` (walking up to `.claude/harness.json`, as the mod does), or the mod prefers CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
